toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise in VA-220 failures traces to Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not to the new installers or firmware 4.2. Brenmoor's lab matched claims to valve source, installer and firmware. Pellacott valves fail at about the same rate (roughly 41–42 per 1,000) whichever installer or firmware is involved. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 per 1,000 everywhere. Unused Pellacott 2026 valves from the warehouse leak at the seat 11% of the time, against 1% for Pellacott's 2025 valves and none for Durrant-Hale. Teardowns show deformed, unseated slide seals.

The independent calibration visit shows Pellacott's leak-test rig was out of service from 9 Jan 2026. No VA-220 test program was loaded on any other rig. Certificate tables repeat four sequences that also appear in November 2025 certificates. So the certificates are very likely not records of real tests, and the score gain came from complete-looking paperwork.

Next steps: keep the six lots on hold and quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott stock. Suspend dock-to-stock. Run Brenmoor's own helium testing, and use Durrant-Hale for supply cover. Do not release lots on fresh certificates, and do not penalise installers. Audit test evidence at other suppliers. The seal and Line 3 effects are not yet separated, so changing the seal source now is premature.
